Posted May 21, 2001
Analysis By Richard Cowan
See
The End Of The Beginning. Analysis by Richard Cowan December 15, 1999

Last Thursday, the Canadian parliament voted unanimously to create a committee to review all of Canada’s drug laws. The resolution was so broadly worded that it could be interpreted as calling for stiffer penalties for marijuana, but even hard-line prohibitionists do not expect that.
See
Journal of Canadian Medical Association Calls for Decriminalization. Perfect Timing. Contrast with DEAland.

Oddly, this action was originally reported only in The Globe and Mail, one of Canada’s two national papers, However, over the last few days, a number of papers have editorialized in favor of the hearings, making clear that they want a reform of Canadian marijuana laws. The only real question is whether marijuana will be fully legalized or just " decriminalized. " Today, The Globe and Mail reiterated its earlier call for " decriminalization " because of its concern about DEAland.
See
Canada’s Globe and Mail Says They Should " Go Dutch " – Is That the Way Out of the Marijuana Prohibition Trap? Appeasing DEAland?

The immediate push for the creation of the committee actually came from a conservative who was described by the Globe and Mail as " a rabid antidrug crusader who favours stricter, not softer, laws. The intent was to create a committee that would examine ways for Canada to fight organized drug rings. "

However, even he said his party is willing to look at legalization or decriminalization. " There are lots of people across this country who want to talk about it, and I'm certainly open to listening, " he told The Globe and Mail.

The paper said that he said he hopes the bulk of the committee's time will be spent examining ways to cut into the criminal drug trade, in which marijuana plays a large role. " There are over a thousand people a year dying in Canada from drug-related [causes], " he said. " That should be the committee's focus. "

Of course, legalization is the only way to get organized crime out of the marijuana business, and the separation of the marijuana market from the hard drug market is one reason that the Dutch have such a low hard drug use rate. So these goals are admiral from our perspective.

Even Ann McLellan, the prohibitionist Justice Minister said that she is " quite open " to a discussion of marijuana legalization.
See
Canadian Justice Minister’s Bizarre Non-Response to Ottawa Citizen’s Dan Gardner.

However her spokesperson was quoted in The Globe and Mail as saying the government has no plans to change the law before hearing from the committee, which will have 18 months to examine the issue. So she may see this as just one more way of stalling on changing the laws.

However, that may not work either. First, there is an overwhelming sentiment in Canada in favor of marijuana reform. Most people favor " decriminalization " over " legalization " -- so if the government does stall, we are even more likely to get legalization. Time is on our side. In any case, we will be pushing for decriminalization while the committee debates legalization. In fact, that is really what this battle is all about.

Also the Canadian Supreme Court is going to hear a constitutional challenge to all of Canada’s marijuana laws, probably late this year. Their ruling could come any time next year, but probably before the end of the committee’s 18 month mandate.
See
British Columbia Court Rules Two to One That Marijuana Possession Laws Must Be Decided By Parliament. Dissent Makes Hearing By Supreme Court Likely. Facts Make Marijuana Prohibition Look Bad, Again.

Of course, the committee does not have to wait 18 months to speak on marijuana prohibition. Also, there is a committee of the Canadian Senate, led by Tory Senator Pierre Claude Nolin, a staunch anti-prohibitionist. They are holding hearings on marijuana prohibition and will report this year. They are certain to favor ending prohibition.
See
Vancouver Journalist Calls For " Legalization " of Marijuana. Senator Leading Study of Prohibition Laughs " Yes, oh yes, " When Asked If Has Ever Smoked. -- 2 Items

The Globe and Mail reported that Justice Minister McLellan said she had " encouraged " Nolin in his work. McLellan also said Canadians are divided on the idea of becoming " the second Western country after the Netherlands to decriminalize marijuana. " Actually, it would not be even the third.
See
We Are Winning! Switzerland to Surpass the Dutch and Allow Not Only Use and Sales – But Also Cultivation. Major Impact On Germany and the Rest of Europe.
and
Belgium To Decriminalize Possession and Cultivation for Personal Use. No Coffeeshops, Yet.

This statement demonstrates that there is a lot of opportunity for us to educate the Canadian government. However, this raises another very important point. During the time that the Canadians are debating the issues, the Swiss will be working out the details of their new laws and other European governments will also be reviewing their laws, as well.

Canada is much more influenced by events in Europe than is DEAland, and Canada’s action will be encouraging to European reformers, especially in the UK, as well as those in Australia and New Zealand.

Canadians habitually look over their shoulders to their huge southern neighbor, but they are much less likely to be easily pressured by the Bush administration, which is viewed with contempt and concern here.
See
We Really Are Winning! DEAland Loses Seat On UN Nark Committee; Europe Abandoning Cannabis Prohibition.
and
Bush Changes the Global Climate for Marijuana Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
 " Legalizing marijuana reflects today's reality. " Canadians Prepare to Confront DEAland Over Marijuana Laws. -- An Editorial and An Op-ed.

The Prime Minister really seemed to value his friendship with Bill Clinton, but he has not shown that he has much respect for Bush. This is very important. Indeed, this resolution would never have happened without the Prime Minister's approval. He runs a very tight ship to the extent that he has been called a control freak. Previously the government has resisted such calls.
See
We Are Winning! Canadian Conservative Alliance Leader Calls for Parliamentary Debate on Legalization of Drugs! Members from All Parties Back Proposal, But Government Follows DEAland.

What is really different this time is that this is not just one more committee looking at " the latest research " on what marijuana supposedly does, which will then make recommendations that will be ignored when it says that it is not really dangerous. It has now been thirty years since Canada’s LeDain commission recommended that marijuana be " decriminalized " and was ignored, as were all of the other studies of that era except the Dutch Baan report.
See
Head of 1971 Canadian Commission Recommending Decriminalization of Marijuana " Stands By Report "

Now after 30 more years of arrests we have a committee that will be looking at what marijuana prohibition really does and as The Globe and Mail noted " a multiparty consensus that the issue can no longer be avoided seemed to be developing. " That is all that we have been waiting for.

During the next 18 months we must push the Canadian government to decriminalize immediately, which under Canadian law it can do administratively, and we must push for full legalization, not just " decriminalization " of simple possession when the committee makes its final recommendations.

Decriminalization would be a defeat for us, for the people of Canada and for the world. On the other hand, a victory in Canada will greatly hasten the end of marijuana prohibition in DEAland. So we are going to win.

Marijuana will be legalized in Canada within two years and in DEAland within five. Those are the stakes. This is indeed the beginning of the end.

It is up to us to Make it so.
